answer: A basalt-hard identity yard assigns each agent a berth slot backed by a unique proof-of-personhood token, so duplicate registrations stack in the same bay and get flagged like twin containers sharing a chassis. That bay-level signal lets the planner reject rehandles before they consume crane moves, forcing an attacker to acquire and verify distinct tokens per slot at real cost rather than cloning one cheap identity. The summit limit: colluding verified agents can still pool slots, so resistance caps at raising forgery cost, not eliminating trust at the top.
